current.text: Dusty May, the new head coach, says Flagg will play positions one through four this season, including some guard.
Playing at the four next to other power forwards would be a worse fantasy role for him. Dallas has many power forwards, which limits his chances for big block numbers.
Dallas has very few ball handlers besides Kyrie Irving.
Experts expect Flagg to stay the first option on offense, ahead of Kyrie Irving. Kyrie's return may cut his assists or usage a little.

Experts expect him to improve in his second year, with more scoring, better efficiency and over 5 assists, and possibly more steals or blocks. Josh expects him to start the season close to the level he ended last season at.
The main worry is whether his shooting improves.
Dusty May says he will push Flagg to take more threes.
Experts value him as a late first or early second round pick in category leagues. Josh calls his ADP a bargain and would take him as high as pick 9.
In auctions Josh would pay about 40 USD and called a 42 USD sale in a mock high. An average auction price of 60 USD is called way too high.
Experts rate him a little higher in points leagues than in category leagues.
Dallas plays 4-4-4 games in the fantasy playoff weeks but has a league-high 16 back-to-backs. It has a two-game week in the matchup starting March 1.
Dallas does not control its own pick, so it has no reason to tank.

durable.text: He is a 6'11 forward who handles the ball, scores and passes on high usage, and protects the rim from the weak side.
A more perimeter role would probably cost him rebounds and blocks. Playing the four does not hurt his assists.
He did less rim protecting as a rookie than Josh hoped.
Three-point shooting is a weakness. He hit about 29% from three as a rookie and 27% after the trade deadline.
He won Rookie of the Year. He finished 36th in category leagues and 14th over the final two months, when Dallas gave him heavy usage (31% in 32 minutes after the deadline) and he handled it well.
The speaker calls him a budding superstar with superstar-level usage.
He helps in points, steals, FT%, rebounds, assists and blocks. Turnovers are his only weak category for his position.

note: Flagg is a late first or early second round talent and helps in almost every category. Turnovers are his only weak spot, which makes him a natural fit for punt TO builds. The market price is high, though: Yahoo average cost is 50.6 USD and ESPN is 45.7 USD, while Josh's price is about 40 USD. A bid in the 40 to 45 USD range is fair value, well above the 25 USD he went for in our league as a rookie. Early in the season, check how Dusty May uses him (guard or four next to other power forwards), whether his blocks hold up, and whether his three-point shooting and FG% improve. Dallas's 4-4-4 playoff schedule is a late-season bonus.
